Just a father, his features weary,
Returning from the day's relentless grind,
Carrying scant riches or renown,
As proof of triumphs he has earned,
Yet joyful within because his loved ones
Delight in his arrival and welcome his familiar tone.

Just a father, with four children in his care,
One among ten million men or beyond,
Trudging forward through each day's hard battle,
Enduring the insults and lashes that life delivers,
Without a single complaint of suffering or resentment,
All for those who wait for him back home.

Just a father, lacking wealth or vanity,
Simply a member of the swarming multitude,
Laboring and pushing onward day after day,
Confronting whatever crosses his path,
Holding his tongue when cruel voices judge him,
Enduring every burden out of love for his family.

Just a father, yet he offers everything
To ease the road for his small children,
Performing, with fierce and unyielding bravery,
The very acts his own father once did for him.
These are the words I write down in his honor:
Just a father, but the finest of all men.
outputs.L3:
# Only a Dad

Each day, an ordinary father returns home from work. He brings with him little in the way of wealth or fame, yet he finds something far more valuable waiting for him: the warmth of his family's love and the joy of their welcome. In their embrace, he discovers a richness that money could never buy.

He is but one of millions of men who quietly endure life's hardships and struggles. Without complaint, he shoulders his burdens day after day, driven by a simple and steadfast purpose—the well-being of those who wait for him at home. His sacrifices go largely unnoticed, but they are no less profound for their quietness.

Though he is neither rich nor proud, he faces whatever challenges come his way with quiet determination. When unfair criticism falls upon him, he bears it in silence, choosing patience over protest. His restraint is not weakness but love—a love so deep that he would rather absorb life's injustices than pass them on to those he cherishes.

He gives everything he has to make life easier for his children, holding nothing back. In doing so, he carries on a legacy of devotion, performing the same selfless deeds that his own father once performed for him. Generation after generation, this quiet faithfulness is passed down, a gift of love that endures through time.

And so, though he may be described as "only a dad," these humble words carry the highest praise. For in his steadfast love, his quiet sacrifice, and his unwavering devotion, he stands celebrated as the very best of men.
outputs.L4:
# The Best of Men

Every evening, as the sun sinks low and the day's demands finally loosen their grip, an ordinary man makes his way home. He carries no briefcase full of important papers, no titles that command respect, no wealth to smooth his path. He is not a name that others recognize, nor a figure that draws admiring glances on the street. He is simply a father, returning once again from the endless struggle that fills his days.

The world he moves through is not gentle with him. He labors under burdens that few can see and fewer still would choose to notice. There are the scornful looks of those who measure a person's worth by their possessions or position. There are the quiet humiliations that come with having little, the moments when pride must be swallowed for the sake of putting food on the table. Yet through all of this, he remains silent. He does not complain of his aching body or his weary spirit. He does not speak of the insults he absorbs or the disappointments he carries home hidden beneath a tired smile.

Why does he endure so much without a word of protest? The answer lies in the faces waiting for him behind the door: his children. For them, he bears every hardship without flinching. For them, he sacrifices his own comfort, his own dreams, perhaps even his own dignity in the eyes of a world that judges too quickly and cares too little. His love is not the kind that seeks recognition or reward. It asks for nothing in return. It simply gives, day after day, year after year, quietly and completely.

And here lies the heart of the poem's message. Society may look upon such a man and see nothing remarkable—no achievements to celebrate, no status to admire. By the ordinary measures of success, he is invisible, unremarkable, easily overlooked. But the poem insists that these measures are wrong. In his selfless devotion, in his willingness to suffer so that his children might thrive, in his quiet courage to keep going when others might give up, this humble father reveals a greatness that wealth and fame can never match. He is, in the truest sense, "the best of men."

Through this portrait, the poem celebrates a love that too often goes unnoticed and unthanked. It reminds us that heroism does not always wear a crown or stand upon a stage. Sometimes it arrives home each evening, weary but unbroken, having spent itself entirely for the sake of others. In honoring this everyday father, the poem asks us to recognize the profound and enduring value of paternal love—a love that, in its silent constancy, may be the most precious thing of all.
outputs.L5:
# The Power of the Present Moment

There is a quiet wisdom in understanding that this moment is the **only** one we truly possess. So often we live divided—half of our attention lingering in the past, the other half racing toward what is **coming** next. Yet life, in all its richness, happens right here, in the space we too easily overlook.

## Only This Moment

We spend so much of our energy waiting for the perfect conditions to be happy. We tell ourselves that contentment will arrive **only** when we reach a certain goal, earn a certain amount, or overcome a particular obstacle. But the truth is simpler and more urgent: the present is the **only** ground on which we can actually stand. Everything else is either memory or imagination.

## What Is Coming

Of course, we cannot ignore the future entirely. Planning, hoping, and preparing for what is **coming** gives our lives direction and purpose. There is beauty in anticipation—in the seeds we plant today knowing the harvest is still on its way. The key is to let the future inspire us without allowing it to steal the joy available right now.

## Bringing It All Together

Perhaps the greatest gift we can offer ourselves is **bringing** our full attention to the life in front of us. **Bringing** presence to a conversation, gratitude to a simple meal, and care to the people beside us transforms ordinary days into something meaningful.

In the end, we are always **bringing** something into the world—whether kindness or indifference, hope or fear. When we recognize that this moment is the **only** one guaranteed, and that something new is always **coming**, we learn to live fully: rooted in the now, open to what's next.

counterfactuals.output:
# The Quiet Provider

He rises with the morning's gray,
Before the sun has learned to shine,
No fanfare marks his humble way,
No spotlight, medal, or headline.

His hands are rough, his shoulders worn
From years of lifting more than weight—
The dreams he carries, gently borne,
For those who wait behind his gate.

He never asks for thanks or praise,
No monument bears his good name,
Just steady work through ordinary days,
A love that asks for nothing back, no claim.

He packs a lunch, he checks the car,
He counts the bills with careful eyes,
He knows exactly who they are—
The children sleeping as he tries.

Not rich in gold or wide renown,
But wealthy in the ways that last:
A daughter's smile, a hand-me-down,
A doorway where his shadow's cast.

And when the evening finally comes,
He sits, still tired, but somehow whole,
For in the small and quiet sums
He's given more than gold—his soul.

So here's to fathers, plain and true,
Who build their love in bricks unseen,
Whose greatest work no eyes may view,
Whose hearts are royal, though unqueen'd.

For he's a king in worn-out shoes,
A hero known by very few—
The kind of man the world can lose
And never know how much it knew.

Before the rising sun.

Nor thanks for all his care.

Though praise you'd wave away:
The quiet strength you gave to us
Still guides my steps today.

Thank you for the steady hands,
The heart that never tired—
A simple man, a faithful man,
The father I've admired.

# The Quiet Giant

He never asks for thanks or praise,
Just moves through steady, silent days,
With calloused hands and weary eyes,
He builds our world, he never cries.

Before the sun begins to climb,
He's up and working, right on time,
He trades his rest, he trades his youth,
And asks for nothing but our truth.

He wears the same old coat each year,
So we might have the things held dear,
The shoes we need, the books to read—
He plants himself so we may seed.

He never speaks of what he's lost,
Nor counts the dreams, nor sums the cost,
His sacrifice is soft and slow,
A quiet love we barely know.

And when at night the house grows still,
He checks the doors, he pays the bill,
He tucks away his private fears,
And carries on through all the years.

So here's to you, our steady guide,
The strength we've always felt inside,
The man who gave and never told—
Your gentle heart is worth more than gold.

We see you now, though late it seems,
The father woven through our dreams,
And every step we ever climb,
Was built upon your love and time.
